page: Amazon Web Services c8a.large is an entry-tier compute-optimized virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, the instance supplies 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and an 8 MB L3 cache pool. Advanced CPU instruction set extensions are supported, including AVX-512 vector arithmetic, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware cryptography acceleration via VAES and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 4.0 GB of DDR5 RAM rated at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no bundled local NVMe storage and relies entirely on networked Amazon EBS volumes. Dedicated network baseline throughput is rated at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present.

Benchmark analysis reflects distinct single-threaded computing advantages due to high core frequency and architectural enhancements. In single-core evaluations, the instance records top-tier results in Geekbench 6 (2702.0), stress-ng single-core (3773.68), single-threaded gzip compression (41.44 GB/sec), and text processing. Uncached memory read bandwidth achieves 52.84 GB/sec, while write operations reach 34.83 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput and compile workloads scale lower due to the two-core ceiling, yielding average marks in Geekbench multi-core (4867.0) and lower percentiles in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Architecturally, c8a.large presents cost-effective compute performance for workloads bound by single-core speed rather than massive parallel scaling. The instance is suited for batch processing, web serving frontends, API gateways, light Redis caching, and single-threaded data transformations.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro System, featuring a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs. Configured with 4.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, it provides 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside an 8 MB L3 cache. Vector processing is reinforced by AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets. The server contains no local storage or GPUs, utilizing networked storage volumes and providing a 1 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-core processing capabilities, leading to top-tier scores in single-threaded compression and Geekbench single-core tests, balanced by average multi-core and memory sub-scores. This profile makes c8a.large an efficient platform for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks, lightweight web serving, microservices, and dedicated API processing.
